definition: A self-supervised learning approach that trains a model to pull representations of similar/related examples closer together and push dissimilar examples apart in embedding space.
details: Contrastive learning is widely used to train embeddings without requiring explicit labels, by constructing positive pairs (e.g., an image and its caption) and negative pairs from unlabeled data.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Contrastive Learning.
